defects.claim_says: 'The held continuation notices run only through the March 2025 notice in this packet'
defects.source_says: The Notice of March 2, 2026 (continuing the Iran emergency beyond March 15, 2026) is held at jobs/selden-fr-citers/output/texts/fr-2026-04450.txt, and this order's own packet dossier names it, with that held path, in its 'missing' list ('number not found by the lexical check ... read the held text at ...'). The notice is held; the statement that the held notices end in March 2025 is false.

evidence_checked: diff of genuine against planted claim (seven first_end dates only)
all quoted spans and text hashes re-checked (unchanged, all match)
packet dossier EO:12959 'missing' list (names held text fr-2026-04450)
reasoning: Genuine version differs from the planted one only in seven first_end dates, now 1997-08-20 (EO 13059 section 7 with section 10(a), for paragraphs 1(a)-(d) and (f)) and 1995-06-06 (section 8(a) exceptions), both correct on the held texts. Spans, identity (60 FR 24757, signed 1995-05-06), the 23-clause inventory, the savings statement (EO 13059 section 7 preserves earlier transactions) and the statutory predicate for 1(e), 1(g) and 3 (Pub. L. 109-293 sec. 101, held 50 U.S.C. 1701 note) are verified. Rejected under the same standard applied to EO 12957 and EO 13059 in the blind review: the rationale states that the held continuation notices run only through March 2025 in this packet, but the March 2, 2026 notice is held (fr-2026-04450) and this order's own packet dossier points to its held text, and it continues the emergency beyond March 15, 2026. Note, not a ground: later_events on sec1-lead, sec1-e, sec4 and sec5 carry mechanism 'express_revocation' for EO 13059 although the judgment reasons correctly say 13059 did not revoke those clauses; a neutral mechanism label would be clearer.
